Glossary

Legal notice: what is it, and what must it contain?

The legal notice is a page on your website that says who is responsible for it: the company name, its contact details, its registration numbers and the web host. In France, every business website must have one.

The definition in one sentence

It is the site's official ID card. It lets any visitor know who they are dealing with, and contact you if needed. It is usually reached through a discreet link at the bottom of every page.

What it usually contains

For a business, you will most often find:

  • The name or company name, and the legal form.
  • The address of the head office or premises.
  • An email address and a phone number to reach you.
  • The registration number, for example the SIREN or the number in the relevant register.
  • The EU VAT number, if you have one.
  • The name of the publishing director, the person answerable for the content.
  • The name, address and contact details of the web host.

Some regulated professions have extra information to show, such as the professional body or chamber they belong to.

What it does for a small business

Beyond the legal duty, it is a question of trust. A customer who is unsure about ordering will sometimes check that there is a real business behind the site. An empty or missing page raises doubts.

A real-life example

A jewellery maker launches her online shop and copies the legal notice from another site, changing only the name. The web host listed is not hers, and the address is that of her old company. A wary customer notices and tells her. A wrong notice looks worse than a short but accurate one.

What you need to know

  • Legal notice, privacy policy and terms of sale are three different things. An online shop needs all three.
  • It must stay up to date: a move, a change of legal status or of web host should be reflected there.
  • A sole trader working from home should in principle give an address. Business address services exist so you do not have to show your home address.

For a special case or a regulated profession, check with your chamber of commerce or trades, or with a legal professional. This page gives pointers, not legal advice.

Your questions

What is the risk of having no legal notice?

Having no legal notice on a business website is a breach that can be penalised. Above all, it sends a bad signal to visitors trying to find out who you are.

Where should the link to the legal notice go?

At the bottom of every page, in the footer. It should be easy to find from anywhere on the site.
